After a wave of intensive real estate expansion swept through the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its business footprint in Sunnyvale. Below is the full report.

Apple continues to expand its business locations

According to a report by The Mercury News (republished via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building at 580 North Mary Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal marks Apple's first major real estate move in the area in 2026; back in 2025, the company had already invested over US$1 billion to expand its operations across the South Bay.

The previous round of expansion included the US$166.9 million purchase of the three-building Cupertino Gateway complex, the US$350 million acquisition of the two-building Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale, and the US$365 million purchase of the adjacent four-building Mathilda Campus.

Apple subsequently invested a further US$216 million to acquire two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its total Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Returning to Apple's new lease — The Mercury News noted that the deal comes amid a renewed pickup in South Bay office leasing activity, with vacancy rates improving on both a quarterly and annual basis:

According to a Colliers report, the South Bay office vacancy rate in the second quarter of 2026 stood at 14.1%. Colliers defines the market as covering Santa Clara County and Fremont. This figure represents an improvement from the 14.8% vacancy rate recorded in the fourth quarter of October to December 2025, as well as the 16.2% vacancy rate in the second quarter of 2025.

Apart from Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
